Not many people on the left are shedding tears after Sen. John Fetterman (D-Penn.) said he’d consider leaving the Democratic Party if Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) was named Senate majority leader over Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.).

“It would be troubling if my caucus elects someone like Van Hollen that has really made his name being very anti-, hostile to Israel,” he said on Fox News on Saturday.

Fetterman makes regular appearances on the conservative network, where he often criticizes the progressive wing of the Democratic Party. In September, Fetterman appeared at the Republican midterm convention via video. That’s led to speculation that he plans to jump ship. President Donald Trump has even urged him to do so.

“I’m a lifelong Democrat who votes overwhelmingly with my party — and should the Senate flip in November, I will still be the 51st vote that I ran on,” he said in September after that convention appearance.

As a 51st vote in a closely divided Senate, Fetterman could have potentially held great sway over his party ― and even solely flipped the chamber back to the GOP if he switched sides. Instead, he will likely be vote number 56, given that Mary Peltola now appears likely to win her race in Alaska.
